features.name: One Person Companies (OPC)
features.oneLine: Runs a one-person company's outward deals: counterparties, scoped engagements, data rooms, approval envelopes and work modules.
features.maturityEvidence: Owner set shipped (2026-10-13). Earlier scan notes: The owner surfaces are mounted at magician-bin/src/main.rs:13354-13374 and the reader at main.rs:12056. Outward sends are recorded but not performed by default (outward_actions.capture_only: true, magician-config.yaml:2468). The C-suite autonomous set is described as 'a bet, not a shipped product' (docs/components/magician/autonomous-agents.md:56).

Re-checks live engagement authority before dispatch

tour.title: Register the counterparty
tour.say: The owner records a counterparty and its identities, so every later deal, room and message resolves to one known relationship rather than a raw address.

tour.title: Open an engagement
tour.say: Opening an engagement grants a bounded, expiring tool ceiling and delegation team for one counterparty, and it never exceeds what the agent already holds.

tour.title: Authority checked live
tour.say: Before an engagement-scoped run dispatches, its authority is read live, so a narrowed or revoked engagement stops the work right away.

tour.title: Standing approval envelopes
tour.say: A standing approval envelope can pre-authorise bounded outward communication; the gate checks each dispatch against it and records why anything falls outside.

tour.title: Share a data room
tour.say: Issuing a room link first records a disclosure for every visible document, so a grant whose record failed is refused instead of silently given.

tour.title: Counterparty opens the room
tour.say: The counterparty presents the link outside the owner's protected API; access is logged first, then only documents that identity may see are served.

tour.title: Run a work module
tour.say: Composable work modules open tracked runs for a deal, collecting declared fields, open gaps and expectations against the same audience reference.

features.name: Public agents (public chat / Envoy)
features.oneLine: Answers strangers on Telegram, WhatsApp and email through a sandboxed envoy agent, while the owner keeps a private control channel.

The shipped bots tag public traffic (skillshub/bots/telegram/src/index.ts:90, skillshub/bots/kapso/src/index.ts:76). The feature map lists it at docs/features/README.md:71.

Selects public-chat policy by source surface

tour.title: Message arrives publicly
tour.say: An ordinary Telegram or Kapso message without the control prefix is tagged as envoy chat and placed on its own per-sender thread.

tour.title: Bot requests a session
tour.say: The bot asks the server for the active session, passing channel, address, verification status and whether the user typed the control prefix.

tour.title: Choose the lane
tour.say: Routing picks a lane: non-control messages go to the guest envoy, verified allowlisted owners keep full trust, and everyone else fails closed.

tour.title: Owner check fails closed
tour.say: Owner status needs an allowlisted address and a transport that authenticated the sender, so unauthenticated email from the owner's address stays a guest.

tour.title: Bind the envoy agent
tour.say: The first guest message creates a session bound to the envoy agent, and later messages reuse it, so each stranger stays isolated.

tour.title: Chat-only public turns
tour.say: Public chat surfaces match a policy with no tools, delegation or handover, so guests get conversation only unless they use the control prefix.

features.name: Relentless (work quality)
features.oneLine: Keeps improving a draft or media artifact within a budget until independent critics accept it, then hands it off.
features.maturityEvidence: Owner confirmed complete (2026-10-13). Doc caveats found by the scan, kept for reference: Native and API suites pass, and paid image and video regeneration is qualified live (docs/components/magician/relentless.md:30-66). Live promotion, canary and adoption of guidance 'remains unverified', and communication remains local draft/capture (relentless.md:70-80).

locations.why: Mounts runs, campaigns, guidance and review routes
Service entry for an owner draft run
Freezes contract and budget at admission
Spawns the controller worker for a run
One actor, critics and decision pass
Critic verdict with scores and findings
Quality view inside the Work page

uiSurface.description: Work page, Quality and review view

tour.title: Start a quality run
tour.say: The owner proposes a draft with criteria and a budget, and the server starts a quality run attached to that piece of work.

tour.title: Freeze the contract
tour.say: Admission freezes the criteria, model pins and maximum spend, so the run cannot quietly change its rules or exceed what the owner approved.
tour.evidence: magician/src/config.rs:2220-2226 ('admitted contracts never change on reload')

tour.title: Actor makes a candidate
tour.say: Each pass asks the actor for a new candidate, seals its bytes, and sends those sealed bytes to independent critic models for review.

tour.title: Critics score it
tour.say: Critics return a verdict with per-criterion scores and findings, and their defects can trigger a regeneration inside the same run and budget.

tour.title: Code decides, not models
tour.say: Deterministic code, not a model, decides whether to retain, accept or stop the candidate, taking the remaining budget into account.

tour.title: Spend reserved first
tour.say: Every paid operation reserves money first and settles against a provider receipt; unknown outcomes keep their reservation and block further paid calls.

tour.title: Owner reviews in Work
tour.say: Accepted artifacts appear in the Work page's quality view for the owner to review, and acceptance and delivery stay separate owner-controlled steps.

features.name: Notes
features.oneLine: Markdown notes that you and your agents write, search, link and publish tasks into, stored wherever you choose.
features.maturityEvidence: The feature map lists Notes, notes search, save-selection and task pages (docs/features/README.md:150-153). Web, Magios and Android surfaces are listed there.

tour.title: Choose where notes live
tour.say: Each workspace picks a notes provider and root folder, and changing it only redirects new notes without ever deleting existing ones.

tour.title: Browse the library
tour.say: The Notes page shows a folder tree and an editor, and reads and saves markdown files through the notes API.

tour.title: Edit and save
tour.say: Saving writes the markdown back to the chosen provider root, so notes stay ordinary files the user can also open elsewhere.

tour.title: Search reads fresh
tour.say: Search reads a fresh snapshot of the notes tree, so an edit made outside the app shows up on the very next query.

tour.title: Save a selection
tour.say: Highlighting text and choosing save to notes files the selection along with the title and link of the page it came from.

tour.title: Publish task pages
tour.say: Completed tasks can be published as note pages, by hand or automatically, giving a readable record that lives outside the task store.

tour.title: Promote to memory
tour.say: A published task note can be offered to memory as a candidate, instead of silently becoming a remembered fact.

features.name: Tasks (V3 task store) and the Work page

Reduces state changes into on-disk files
Agent saves state for next run
Marks activity on or off plan

tour.title: Create a task
tour.say: A task arrives through the version-three task API from chat, the Work page, a schedule or an agent, always scoped to the authenticated workspace.

tour.title: Write the manifest
tour.say: The service writes the task manifest and state, marking it persistent or internal so background work stays off the main task list.

tour.title: Plan before running
tour.say: Tasks can be planned first; plans are versioned, can ask clarifying questions, and may need the owner's approval before execution.

tour.title: Start an execution
tour.say: Starting execution creates a run under the task, which agents carry out, handing sub-work to the delegation dispatcher when they need help.

tour.title: Durable state on disk
tour.say: Every state change is reduced into files on disk, so tasks, executions and outputs survive restarts and can be inspected later.

tour.title: Project the progress
tour.say: Progress summaries capture status, attention needs and available outputs, and these feed live updates to the feed and connected clients.

tour.title: One Work page
tour.say: The Work page composes tasks, monitors, internal work, crew, attention and quality views over these same APIs without adding a new store.

features.name: Autonomous harness (plane, coding engines, harness engines)
features.oneLine: Lets agents work unattended on schedules and drive external coding CLIs through a governed tool plane.
features.maturityEvidence: Owner confirmed complete (2026-10-13). Doc caveats found by the scan, kept for reference: Seven agents fire on schedules, but the C-suite set is 'a bet, not a shipped product' (docs/components/magician/autonomous-agents.md:38-57). The Claude, Grok, Antigravity and Pi coding engines are listed in docs/features/README.md:110-113.

Loads program charter and runtime state
Routes a turn to a harness engine

Promotes a backlog item to work

uiSurface.description: Settings engines panel; Work page Company loop view

tour.title: Declare a schedule
tour.say: An agent becomes autonomous by declaring a schedule and focus areas, each pointing at a written charter, with no separate enable switch.

tour.title: Scheduler picks it up
tour.say: The server reconciles scheduler entries from those declarations, so each focus area fires on its own cron schedule as a separate cycle.

tour.title: Load the program
tour.say: Each cycle loads the program charter and its runtime state, so the standing instructions live in the store rather than in code.

tour.title: Pick a harness engine
tour.say: When a harness engine is configured, the turn goes to a named external engine such as Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Grok or Antigravity.

tour.title: Mint a plane grant
tour.say: Magician mints a short-lived grant and gives the engine an MCP configuration pointing back at itself, so every tool call returns through Magician.

tour.title: Every call is governed
tour.say: Each tool call is authorized against the grant, and revocation is checked again just before the action runs, so stale grants cannot slip through.

tour.title: Continue or stop
tour.say: After a cycle, the harness decides whether to continue within budget and classifies anomalies, so hollow or stuck runs come up for repair.

features.name: Apps (App Platform)
features.oneLine: Installs reviewed app packages that add tools, workflows, pages and widgets, each running under granted, jailed authority.
features.maturityEvidence: Owner set experimental (2026-10-13). Earlier scan notes: The archived design 'records the completed program', but 'remaining operator evidence is maintained in whattotest.md' (docs/components/magician/app-platform-truth-baseline.md:9-11, 52-54). System packages are admitted at boot (magician-config.yaml:1548-1554).

Renders app pages in the web UI
Picks the widget for a slot

tour.title: Import a package
tour.say: An app arrives as a package whose manifest declares its tools, workflows, surfaces and limits, and it is staged for review rather than enabled.

tour.title: Owner reviews it
tour.say: The owner sees an installation review listing exactly which tools, memory reads and workflow grants the app is asking for.
tour.evidence: installation_review.rs:173-230 (reviewed tool runtime, memory read, workflow grant)

tour.title: Approve and enable
tour.say: Approving moves the installation through its lifecycle to enabled; later it can be disabled, quarantined, updated, rolled back or purged.

tour.title: Bind app tools
tour.say: When an agent calls an app tool, the call is planned against the tool's declared shape and containment profile before anything is dispatched.

tour.title: Run an action
tour.say: Actions can also be invoked directly, producing a run whose status is projected from the ordinary task store rather than a separate state machine.

tour.title: Jailed execution
tour.say: App code runs inside an operating-system jail with reviewed artifacts and egress rules, so it cannot reach beyond what was granted.

tour.title: Surfaces in the UI
tour.say: Approved apps render their own pages, widgets and slots in the web app through sandboxed surface hosts that the owner reviewed.

tour.say: Typing at-vibedev with a request in ordinary chat, or saying start a vibedev build, is recognised as a request to start a build.

tour.title: Divert the chat turn
tour.say: After saving the user's message and before any model call, the chat turn is diverted into the VibeDev rail instead of producing a reply.

tour.title: Resolve and decide
tour.say: The rail resolves which project is meant, then decides whether to start the build, refuse it, or ask the user to choose a project.

tour.title: Admit and dispatch
tour.say: The run service durably admits the build, creates a task owned by the lead coding agent, and dispatches it for execution.

tour.title: Pick a coding engine
tour.say: A coding profile decides which engine runs the build, such as Pi, Claude Code, Codex, Grok or Antigravity, within budget and sandbox rules.

tour.title: Sandbox approvals
tour.say: Writing outside the sandbox needs an owner approval, and paths inside Magician's own installation are refused when write paths are validated.

tour.title: Studio, preview, deploy
tour.say: The studio shows runs, logs, checkpoints and diffs, starts live previews, and can merge, open pull requests, or deploy the project.

features.name: Monitors

tour.title: Activate as a task
tour.say: Confirming creates an ordinary scheduled task with a monitor contract attached; there is no second scheduler, queue or store.

tour.title: Validate the spec
tour.say: The contract is validated and normalised before saving, and later contract edits bump a server-owned monitor revision.

tour.title: Baseline, then compare
tour.say: The first run records a quiet baseline, and failed source reads never count as changes, so an unreadable page cannot look like deletions.

tour.title: Notify only on change
tour.say: Each update is checked for suppression reasons, so unchanged runs never notify and a dismissed change stays quiet until something different appears.

tour.title: Today and Needs you
tour.say: Material changes show up as Today cards, while repeated source failures raise a needs-access item that clears itself after a clean read.

tour.title: Manage anywhere
tour.say: Users pause, resume, run now, edit, convert tasks and give feedback from the web, iOS or chat, all acting on the same task.

features.name: Contextual assistance
features.oneLine: A single Option-key tap anywhere offers rewrite, reply, summarize or task actions on what you're looking at, inserted in place.

tour.title: Watch the target
tour.say: A native Accessibility watcher on the Mac notices what you are working on, whether a selection, a text field, a web page or Finder files.

tour.title: Never a dead end
tour.say: If nothing text-like is found, the frontmost window becomes the context, while password fields and excluded apps are suppressed entirely.

tour.title: Offer fitting actions
tour.say: A single left Option tap opens a menu whose actions come from the backend catalog, with a local copy used if the server is unreachable.

tour.title: Run the action
tour.say: The chosen action, with its text, page, app and optional screenshot context, goes to the contextual writing endpoint, which drafts the result.

tour.title: Or file a task
tour.say: Task and follow-up actions create real tasks in the same thread, using the draft as the task description.

tour.title: Insert in place
tour.say: Pressing Tab pastes the draft where you were after re-checking focus, then restores your clipboard; if focus moved, nothing is pasted.

tour.say: Each channel runs as a supervised per-scope bot process that the owner starts, stops, restarts and inspects from the Channels page.

tour.title: Receive a message
tour.say: Platform adapters receive incoming messages, and Kapso checks the webhook signature against the exact raw body before parsing anything.

tour.title: Enroll the sender
tour.say: Channel identities enroll through the bot, and the owner can approve, check status or revoke them through the enrollment endpoints.

tour.say: The shared channel runtime turns each inbound message into a Magician chat message, choosing an owner-control or public thread from the prefix.

tour.title: Replies flow back
tour.say: Replies, task updates and critical alerts come back over the realtime connection, and the adapter sends them out on the platform.

tour.title: Auth problems surface

Alert card sent to devices and bots

tour.title: Something needs you
tour.say: When an agent needs input, approval, a clarification or a decision, it raises one canonical ask instead of guessing.

tour.title: Spot outward actions
tour.say: Before executing, each action is classified, and anything that can send email, messages or invitations, including raw passthrough arguments, counts as outward.

tour.title: Capture by default
tour.say: By default an outward action is recorded but not performed, so the whole system can be rehearsed without reaching a real third party.

tour.title: Check the recipient
tour.say: Outward sends must name their recipients and fit the bound work context, otherwise the gate refuses them before anything leaves.

tour.title: Deliver the ask
tour.say: A delivery coordinator routes critical asks as alert cards to channels and devices, tracking a claim and a report for each delivery.

tour.title: Answer once
tour.say: The owner answers through one endpoint from Attention, chat, a bot or a phone, and the waiting work resumes with that answer.

features.name: Secrets and vault
features.oneLine: Stores credentials encrypted per workspace and injects them into tool calls without the model ever seeing them.
features.maturityEvidence: Listed as 'Secret vault' in docs/features/README.md:162, with a /vault UI route and vault routes in secret_vault_api.rs:763-792.

tour.title: Add a secret
tour.say: The owner adds a credential on the Vault page, and the server stores it in the workspace's encrypted secret store.

tour.title: Keychain-backed key
tour.say: Encryption keys come from a platform key provider such as the macOS Keychain, which is set up when the secret runtime boots.

tour.title: Agents ask the broker
tour.say: Agents can list available secrets and request a credential through a broker, and some requests wait for the owner's approval.

tour.title: Inject at dispatch
tour.say: Secret references in an action are resolved and injected just before execution, and unresolved references stop the action from running.

tour.title: Only approved sinks
tour.say: Credentials may only flow into recognised sinks, such as specific HTTP parameters, and other destinations are refused while the action is prepared.

tour.title: Scrub the results
tour.say: Tool results are sanitised so that any known secret value is removed before the output goes back to the agent.

features.name: Skills hub and skills

tour.say: Tool skills become capability packs that agents can call, wrapped with spend gates when a skill declares paid usage.

tour.title: Activate playbooks
tour.say: Procedure skills are activated on demand, loading their instructions and any helper scripts as ephemeral tools for the current run.

tour.title: Install and run
tour.say: From the Skills page the owner browses the catalog, installs or uninstalls skills, edits their environment and runs actions directly.

tour.title: Learn your style

tour.say: Transcribed turns are written into a chat thread tied to the meeting, so the conversation can be read while it happens.

tour.title: Speak into the call
tour.say: A responder, which can be a realtime voice model, decides what to say and streams spoken replies back into the call.

tour.title: Summarize and remember
tour.say: A summarizer condenses the transcript, and a scoped memory writer stores the summary so it can be recalled later.

features.name: Voice (live calls, dictation, speech)
features.oneLine: Talk to Magician in live voice calls, dictate notes, and hear spoken replies through configurable speech providers.
features.maturityEvidence: Live voice call mode, dictation and TTS are listed in docs/features/README.md:133-138. A single control websocket serves every provider (magician-bin/src/main.rs:13660-13668).

locations.why: Fans task results into the call

uiSurface.description: Live call panel, desktop Ambient Orb, /warroom

tour.title: Start a call
tour.say: The user starts a live voice call from the web panel or desktop orb, which opens one control websocket whatever the provider is.

tour.title: Orchestrator starts
tour.say: The voice orchestrator starts a realtime session with the configured provider and sets call boundaries that ground each turn of the conversation.

tour.title: Was it for me
tour.say: An addressing check decides whether speech was directed at the assistant, so background talk does not trigger replies.

tour.title: Tools from voice
tour.say: When the voice model calls a tool, the dispatcher runs it through Magician and returns a structured status to the conversation.

tour.title: Results fan back
tour.say: Longer work, such as delegated chat or completed tasks, is fanned back into the live call as spoken updates.

tour.title: Keep long calls alive
tour.say: Long calls can rotate to a fresh provider session for a recorded reason, so the conversation continues past provider session limits.

tour.title: Dictation and speech
tour.say: Outside calls, dictated voice notes are transcribed and saved, and replies can be spoken aloud through the text-to-speech endpoint.

features.name: Developer Mode Workbench (PTY)
features.oneLine: A developer mode that runs CLIs like Claude Code in real terminals inside a chat thread, with live diffs.
features.maturityEvidence: Listed in docs/features/README.md:109, with full mechanics in docs/components/magician/developer-mode-workbench.md.

tour.title: Switch to dev mode
tour.say: A thread can switch from chat to developer mode, which replaces the chat canvas with a workbench while keeping the same thread and events.

tour.title: Pick a CLI
tour.say: The launcher lists installed command-line runtimes and directories, so the owner chooses which CLI to start and where it runs.

tour.title: Spawn a terminal
tour.say: Starting a session spawns a real pseudo-terminal hosted in tmux, so it behaves like the bare CLI and can persist across reloads.

tour.title: Track live sessions
tour.say: Each workspace keeps a registry of live sessions with replay buffers, so reopening the page restores what was on the screen.

tour.title: Stream the bytes
tour.say: Terminal output streams to the browser as live chunk events, while text typed in the composer is written to the session as keyboard input.

tour.title: See the changes
tour.say: A diff endpoint summarises what the CLI changed in the repository, using three git commands no matter how many files changed.

features.name: Work Evidence Graph
features.oneLine: Turns finished work, browsing, screen activity and meetings into reviewable evidence and entities for reports and reviews.
features.maturityEvidence: 'Evidence and entity review' is listed in docs/features/README.md:90-91, with a design in docs/components/magician/work-evidence-graph.md and a /evidence route.

tour.title: Distill finished work
tour.say: After work finishes, its episode is distilled into an evidence record describing what happened, with source references and a producer tag.

tour.title: Other producers too
tour.say: Browsing, screen observations and meetings feed the same kind of record, clustered first so only salient activity becomes evidence.

tour.title: Faceted, not typed
tour.say: Each record gets open-vocabulary facets with a confidence, proposed by the model and overridable by the user, instead of fixed domain types.

tour.title: Link entities
tour.say: People, projects and other entities are extracted and merged, and co-occurrence views show which entities tend to appear together.

tour.title: Write grounded reviews
tour.say: Reviews are synthesised from a window of evidence and then checked for citation coverage, so each claim points back to records.

tour.title: Correct and review
tour.say: On the evidence page the user browses records and entities, corrects mistakes and gives feedback that improves later reviews.

features.name: Content sources and readers
features.oneLine: One provider-neutral way for agents, feeds and monitors to search and read web, RSS, browser and app sources.
features.maturityEvidence: 'Provider-neutral content acquisition' is listed in docs/features/README.md:104, with the contract in docs/components/magician/content-sources.md.
routes: no HTTP routes; agent tools content_search, content_read, authorize_content_read

tour.title: Agent searches
tour.say: An agent calls the content search tool, and the request is resolved against the workspace's content acquisition settings and registered sources.

tour.title: Discover candidates
tour.say: Discovery adapters such as RSS, public web search or app capabilities return cheap candidate records before anything is fully fetched.

tour.title: Rank before fetching
tour.say: Each candidate carries identity, title, link, timestamps, privacy and a content hash, so ranking happens before any expensive read.

tour.title: Reads need a reason
tour.say: Feed and monitor reads must include selection evidence naming their source, so a read can never pass itself off as a privileged internal one.

tour.title: Fetch safely
tour.say: The public fetcher validates addresses, pins DNS on every hop, sends no credentials and bounds the response size before returning a document.

tour.title: Browser when needed
tour.say: When a page needs rendering or a signed-in session, a browser reader can take over retrieval from the plain web fetcher.

features.name: Delivery receipts
features.oneLine: Checks what really happened to sent messages, whether delivered, bounced or complained about, instead of trusting 'sent'.
features.maturityEvidence: Code review 2026-10-13: the parts are built and tested (126 tests). The receipt worker starts at boot, the maildir bounce pull, the ledger and suppressions all exist, and suppressions are checked before sending (executor.rs:51798). But no channel registers live sends in the sent index (only POST /delivery/sent writes it, and nothing calls it: delivery.md:122-128), and the intake does not resolve a missing act_ref, so bounces stay uncorrelated without manual input. No provider webhooks, no UI.

tour.title: Remember what was sent
tour.say: Each live send is registered in a sent-message index under its provider message identifier, so later receipts can be matched back to it.

tour.title: Pull bounce mail
tour.say: A deployment can name a bounce mailbox, and a puller reads delivery status notices from it, because no provider pushes receipts unprompted.

tour.title: Read the notice
tour.say: Delivery status notices are parsed per recipient into states such as delivered, failed, soft bounce, hard bounce or complaint.

tour.title: Admit the receipt
tour.say: The intake attributes each receipt to the original act and scope, and records every attempt so the evidence stays auditable.

tour.title: Order-independent fold
tour.say: States are folded by severity, keeping the most serious, so the order in which webhooks arrive can never change the final answer.

tour.title: Feed suppression
tour.say: Hard bounces and complaints then become suppression entries through delivery hygiene, so the system stops writing to people who cannot or will not receive.

features.name: Ask loop (planner clarifications)
features.oneLine: When a plan is missing details, asks targeted clarifying questions within a budget, pauses, and resumes with the answers.
features.maturityEvidence: Owner confirmed complete (2026-10-13). Doc caveats found by the scan, kept for reference: V3 task-plan clarification is tried first and the V2 AskLoopApi is a fallback (docs/components/magician/hitl-attention.md:606). Clarifications are one of the canonical HITL sources (hitl-attention.md:16).

locations.why: Decides if a question is worth asking
Registers plan's open inputs as slots

uiSurface.description: Plan inspector clarifications tab; Attention requests

tour.title: Should we ask
tour.say: A budget policy weighs task complexity and the channel to decide whether a question is worth interrupting the user at all.

tour.title: Watch confidence
tour.say: Plan confidence is tracked slot by slot, and a drop below the thresholds triggers a clarification instead of a guess.

tour.title: Write the question
tour.say: A clarifier generates a targeted question from templates and context, describing exactly which detail is blocking progress on the plan.

tour.title: Pause the run
tour.say: The execution pauses, possibly batching several questions together, and the session is saved so nothing is lost while waiting.

tour.title: User answers
tour.say: The answer arrives through the clarification endpoint or the task plan clarification route, from Attention or the plan inspector.

tour.title: Interpret the reply
tour.say: An interpreter classifies the reply as a direct answer, a correction, extra context, a refusal, or several values at once.

tour.title: Resume the work
tour.say: Once answered, the resume service applies the value and resumes the paused execution from where it stopped.

features.name: Scheduling (time negotiation with outsiders)
features.oneLine: Proposes meeting times to outside contacts, absorbs their replies, holds agreed slots, and flags when they go silent.
features.maturityEvidence: Code review 2026-10-13: the negotiation record is built and reachable. It covers open, offer, reply, re-offer, hold, reschedule, close and a silence sweep running at boot (magician-media/src/scheduling, routes at work_modules_api.rs:2880-2990, 78 tests), and the ambassador can use it through the work-modules skill. The calendar side has no production path. There is no free/busy lookup; the offer and hold intents are returned as JSON that nothing executes; the ambassador is denied calendar tools because calendar writes are not in SENDING_ACTIONS (outward_actions.rs:131-145), so no booking is made and no hold released; inbound replies are not routed automatically; and there is no UI.

locations.why: Reply joined by exact message id
Binds a sent offer to negotiation

tour.title: Open a negotiation
tour.say: A negotiation opens for a known counterparty audience with candidate time slots, and resolving who that person is stays the caller's job.

tour.title: Compose the offer
tour.say: The offer comes back as words and times rather than a send, so any channel can deliver it through the normal outward gate.

tour.title: Absorb the reply
tour.say: When the counterparty answers, the reply is read against the open offer and recorded as accepted, declined, or countered with new times.

tour.title: Hold the time
tour.say: Agreeing produces a hold intent describing what a calendar needs, again without naming any channel or calendar provider.

tour.title: Silence is a state
tour.say: If nobody answers, silence is derived from the offer window and ripens into an obligation they owe us, with a due date that stays stable.

features.name: God mode
features.oneLine: Lets trusted agents step outside the shell, file and network sandbox, asking the owner before each new action.
features.maturityEvidence: Off by default: GodModeSettings.enabled has #[serde(default)] (magician/src/config.rs:2263-2266) and the seed config sets god_mode.enabled: false (magician-config.yaml:2193-2194); listed under [Unreleased] in magician/CHANGELOG.md:18; documented in docs/components/magician/god-mode.md. Only trusted agents qualify (god_mode.rs:250), and every uncovered action waits for owner approval, defaulting to deny after 300 s (god_mode.rs:51).

locations.why: Grants session only to trusted runs
Shell refusal routed to god mode

uiSurface.description: A God mode panel at the top of Settings sets the default and can forget all grants; in chat, the composer's presence orb turns it on or off for that chat with a danger halo; approvals arrive as choice cards (allow once, this session, always, deny).

tour.title: Flip the default
tour.say: The owner turns god mode on in Settings. That becomes the default for every chat and for background runs.

tour.title: Per-chat orb switch
tour.say: Clicking the glowing orb in the composer overrides that default for one chat, along with every run the chat starts.

tour.title: Only trusted agents
tour.say: When a run starts, it gets a god mode session only if the agent is trusted and god mode is on for it. Everyone else keeps the normal sandbox.

tour.title: Sandbox says no
tour.say: When the sandbox would refuse a command, the request goes to god mode instead of failing.

tour.title: Read every command
tour.say: A real shell parser picks out every command in the line. Anything it cannot name can only ever be allowed once.

tour.title: Ask the owner
tour.say: If no earlier approval covers the action, the owner gets a card: allow once, for this session, always, or deny. No answer in five minutes counts as deny.

tour.title: Remember the answer
tour.say: Lasting approvals are saved at the scope the owner picked, and all forgotten when the god mode setting changes.

features.name: VibeDev crews
features.oneLine: Splits one coding goal into lanes that build at once, then merges them into one branch.
features.maturityEvidence: No feature flag: magician-bin always starts the crew supervisor at boot and registers the eight crew routes; the web studio rail (CrewSection.svelte) and the iPhone app (VibeDevCrewCard.swift) both show crews. Crews only run on trusted projects. Since deae26fa3 (2026-10-15) the planner sees the base branch's real files and the rail pages finished crews. Push to the iPhone lock screen shipped with coding-runs push (7c93cbbbd); the open follow-up is a per-lane engine choice in the planner (docs/plans/2026-10-12-vibedev-crews-plan.md).

locations.why: POST endpoint that proposes a crew
Planner sees the repo's real files
Committed tree of the base branch
Starts each lane with budget share
Each lane is a trusted run
Studio rail crew form and lanes
Open crews first, finished ones paged

uiSurface.description: The Crews section of the VibeDev studio rail: a goal form (Plan lanes), a status per crew and lane, and Start, Stop, Merge again, Resolve, Pick attempt and Open PR; finished crews fold under Show earlier crews. Start and pull-request questions also appear in Attention and the notch. The iPhone app shows the same crews.

tour.title: One goal, a crew
tour.say: You give the crew one goal for a trusted project. It saves a plan and asks you to start it, in the studio or right from the notch.

tour.title: Splitting into lanes
tour.say: A planner breaks the goal into up to eight lanes. It reads the files actually in the repo first, so each lane gets a short brief and claims real paths, and lanes don't step on each other.

tour.title: Lanes start together
tour.say: Once you say go, every lane starts as its own coding run on its own branch, each with a fair share of the budget.

tour.title: A quiet supervisor
tour.say: In the background, a supervisor wakes whenever a lane finishes and checks every minute too, so a missed event or a restart never leaves the crew stuck.

tour.title: Merging the work
tour.say: When every lane is done, their branches merge in order into one crew branch. If two lanes clash, a helper lane can fix the conflict.

tour.title: One tidy report
tour.say: You get one summary for the whole crew instead of a ping per lane, then a question about opening a pull request.

tour.title: Watching in the studio
tour.say: The studio rail shows crews still in play, each with a status dot for every lane, and folds finished ones away. Open a lane's run, or start, stop, merge and pick a winner right there.
